s1.syndrome_frame: Severe fatigue and muscular weakness with a large tumor on the distal part of the finger, associated with hypercalcemia, hypophosphatemia, and elevated parathyroid hormone
salient_findings: Large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger
Radiographic evidence of bone resorption and multiple fractures
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 60s
History of primary hyperparathyroidism 6 years prior to presentation
Patient refused therapeutic management for primary hyperparathyroidism
Patient is cachectic
Significant muscular weakness
Hypercalcemia at 3.6 mmol/L
Hypophosphatemia at 0.65 mmol/L
Elevated serum parathyroid hormone at 380 pmol/L
Large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger
Radiography showed complete lysis of the underlying phalanx and periosteal bone resorption
Chest radiograph revealed important deformation of the ribs
Thoracic CT scan revealed multiple lesions associated with multiple rib and vertebral fractures
Skull radiography showed pattern of trabecular resorption with 'salt-and-pepper' appearance
Cervical ultrasonography revealed a nodule in right thyroid lobe
Sestamibi parathyroid scintigraphy identified hyperfunctional nodule

shortlist.label: Brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has primary hyperparathyroidism, hypercalcemia, and a tumor on the distal part of the finger with histopathology showing fibrous tissue, woven bone, and giant cells, consistent with a brown tumor

shortlist.label: Primary hyperparathyroidism
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of primary hyperparathyroidism, elevated parathyroid hormone, hypercalcemia, and hypophosphatemia, indicating uncontrolled primary hyperparathyroidism

shortlist.label: Osteitis fibrosa cystica
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has hyperparathyroidism, hypercalcemia, and radiographic findings of bone resorption and cystic changes, consistent with osteitis fibrosa cystica

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor of bone
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a tumor on the distal part of the finger with histopathology showing giant cells, which could be consistent with a giant cell tumor of bone, although the presence of primary hyperparathyroidism and brown tumor is more likely

shortlist.label: Parathyroid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of primary hyperparathyroidism, elevated parathyroid hormone, and a nodule in the right thyroid lobe, which could be consistent with parathyroid carcinoma, although this would be a rare cause of the patient's symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's history of primary hyperparathyroidism, hypercalcemia, hypophosphatemia, and elevated serum parathyroid hormone levels, combined with the presence of a large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger and radiographic findings of bone resorption, are consistent with the diagnosis of a brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism, which is a known complication of untreated primary hyperparathyroidism.

rejected.label: Primary hyperparathyroidism
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of primary hyperparathyroidism, this diagnosis does not specifically explain the tumor on the finger or the radiographic findings of bone resorption.

rejected.label: Osteitis fibrosa cystica
rejected.why: This condition is a skeletal manifestation of hyperparathyroidism, but it does not specifically explain the tumor on the finger.

rejected.label: Giant cell tumor of bone
rejected.why: While the histopathology of the tumor shows giant cells, the clinical and radiographic findings are more consistent with a brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism, which is a specific type of giant cell lesion associated with hyperparathyroidism.

rejected.label: Parathyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence to suggest parathyroid carcinoma, such as a parathyroid gland mass or metastatic disease, and the findings are more consistent with a complication of untreated primary hyperparathyroidism.
